props.gloss_en: 'you shall surely send the mother' -- one you are commanded to send away, excluding this one, which you are commanded not to send but to bring to the treasurer
Ravina: therefore a kosher bird that killed a person is exempt from sending away
what is the reason? the verse says 'you shall surely send the mother' -- one you are commanded to send away, excluding this one, which you are commanded not to send but to bring to court
a case where its sentence was passed
rather, a case where its sentence was not passed, and one must bring it to court to fulfil through it 'and you shall eradicate the evil from your midst'
a case where he had a nest in his house and consecrated it
a case where he merely saw a nest and consecrated it
a case where he lifted the chicks, consecrated them, and returned them
the mishna: if he took the young and returned them to the nest, and afterwards the mother returned onto them, he is exempt from sending
a case where he lifted the mother, consecrated her, and returned her
from the outset he was obligated in sending her away, before he consecrated her

R' Yochanan b. Yosef: consecrated a wild animal and then slaughtered it -- exempt from covering [the blood]; slaughtered it and then consecrated it -- obligated to cover, for he was already obligated in covering before it came to hekdesh
Rav: [the mishna speaks of] one who consecrates the fruits of his dovecote, and they rebelled
Shmuel: [the mishna speaks of] one who consecrates his hen for Temple maintenance
the fruits of his dovecote are altar consecrations; since they are consecrated with inherent sanctity, their sanctity does not lapse from them
a Temple-maintenance consecration -- sanctity of value alone -- once it rebelled, its sanctity lapsed (and it is obligated in sending)
wherever it is, it is in the treasury of the Merciful One, as it is written 'The earth is the Lord's, and its fullness' (Ps 24:1)
and so said R' Yochanan: [the mishna speaks of] one who consecrates his hen for Temple maintenance, and it rebelled
R' Yochanan: 'this maneh is for Temple maintenance', and it was stolen or lost -- he bears responsibility for it until it reaches the treasurer
Reish Lakish: [he is not responsible for the lost maneh] -- wherever it is, it is in the treasury of the Merciful One
R' Yochanan's liability for the maneh is where he said 'upon me'; the hen [that stays consecrated] is where he said 'this is'
by inference, for Reish Lakish, even though he said 'upon me', he is not liable
a vow is one who says 'a burnt offering is upon me', a gift one who says 'this is a burnt offering'; a vow that died, was stolen or lost -- he is responsible for it; a gift -- he is not
that is altar consecrations, which lack sacrifice; but Temple-maintenance consecrations, which do not lack sacrifice -- even though he said 'upon me', he is not liable

the mishna: 'this ox is a burnt offering', 'this house is an offering' -- the ox died, the house fell: he is not responsible; 'this ox is upon me as a burnt offering', 'this house is upon me as an offering' -- the ox died, the house fell: he must pay
Rav Hamnuna: all agree with regard to valuations that even though he said 'upon me', he is not liable
what is the reason? because it cannot be said without 'upon me': how would he say it? 'my valuation' -- upon whom? 'so-and-so's valuation' -- upon whom?

R' Natan: 'and he shall give your valuation on that day, holy to the Lord' (Lev 27:23) -- why stated? since consecrations and tithes redeemed onto non-sacred money carry no responsibility if it is stolen or lost, one might think so here too; the verse says 'and he shall give your valuation' -- it is non-sacred until it reaches the treasurer

Rav Hamnuna (as corrected): all agree with regard to valuations that even though he did not say 'upon me', he is liable, as it is written 'and he shall give your valuation': it is non-sacred in your hand until it reaches the treasurer

objections.gloss_en: אמר ליה רבי שמעון בן לקיש: וכיון שמרדה פקעה לה קדושתה! -- once the hen rebelled, its sanctity lapsed

answered_by.gloss_en: אמר ליה: בבי גזא דרחמנא איתא, דכתיב לה' הארץ ומלואה (= p_bevei_gaza_derachmana)

objections.gloss_en: ורמי דרבי שמעון בן לקיש אדרבי שמעון בן לקיש... קשיא דריש לקיש אדריש לקיש -- of the hen he says its sanctity lapsed, of the maneh that wherever it is, it is in the treasury

answered_by.gloss_en: לא קשיא: הא מקמי דשמעיה מרבי יוחנן רביה, הא לבתר דשמעיה -- the hen statement was before he heard it from R' Yochanan his teacher, the maneh statement after (his retraction at 139a.12)

objections.gloss_en: ורמי דרבי יוחנן אדרבי יוחנן... קשיא דרבי יוחנן אדרבי יוחנן; אלא דרבי יוחנן אדרבי יוחנן קשיא! -- of the hen he says it is in the treasury wherever it is, of the maneh that he is responsible until it reaches the treasurer

answered_by.gloss_en: לא קשיא: הא דאמר עלי, הא דאמר הרי זו (= p_ry_alai_veharei_zo)

objections.gloss_en: והתניא: איזהו נדר ואיזו היא נדבה... נדר -- חייב באחריותה -- one who says 'upon me' is responsible

answered_by.gloss_en: אמר לך ריש לקיש: הני מילי קדשי מזבח דמחוסר הקרבה (= p_rl_kodshei_mizbeach_bilvad)

objections.gloss_en: והתנן: בית זה עלי קרבן -- נפל הבית -- חייב לשלם -- even of Temple-maintenance consecrations, 'upon me' makes him liable

answered_by.gloss_en: הני מילי היכא דמת השור ונפל הבית, דליתנהו; אבל היכא דאיתנהו -- כל היכא דאיתיה בבי גזא דרחמנא איתיה -- he pays where the item no longer exists; where it still exists (lost or stolen), it is in the treasury

objections.gloss_en: מתקיף לה רבא: לימא הריני בערכי, הריני בערך פלוני! -- it can be said without 'upon me'
ועוד, תניא, רבי נתן אומר: ונתן את הערכך... חולין עד שיבאו לידי גזבר -- valuation money carries responsibility until it reaches the treasurer
